      <title>Five EU states announce plans for immigration ‘return hubs’ in Rwanda</title>
      <link>https://www.theguardian.com/world/2026/nov/16/eu-states-immigration-return-hubs-rwanda</link>
      <description><p>Germany, Austria, Netherlands, Denmark and Greece likely to face challenges to policy criticised as ‘grave moral failing’</p><p>Five EU member states have announced plans to set up an offshore centre in Rwanda for people with no legal right to stay in Europe, in a pilot scheme that is expected to face legal challenges and has been denounced as “a grave moral failing”.</p><p>The five countries – Germany, Austria, the Netherlands, Denmark and Greece – are the first to seek to use the EU’s <a href="https://www.theguardian.com/world/2026/mar/26/meps-back-plans-for-return-hubs-raising-fears-of-human-rights-black-holes">newly agreed returns law</a> that allows<em> </em>people who have exhausted all avenues of appeal against their removal from Europe to be sent to a third country.</p> <a href="https://www.theguardian.com/world/2026/nov/16/eu-states-immigration-return-hubs-rwanda">Continue reading...</a></description>

      <title>Delaware hit by rare November tornado</title>
      <link>https://www.theguardian.com/environment/2026/nov/16/delaware-hit-by-rare-november-tornado</link>
      <description><p>Meanwhile, severe thunderstorms bring hailstones the size of baseballs in Argentina</p><p>The National Weather Service in the US has confirmed that an EF1 tornado touched down south-east of Newark in the Salem Woods neighbourhood, Delaware, on Thursday. The tornado reached 160 metres wide, had a path length of 4.4 miles (7.1km) and reached estimated peak winds of up to 100mph (161km/h). There were no injuries or fatalities but windows and roofs were damaged on several homes, a large hotel sign fell on to a number of cars, and a semi truck overturned on I95. Although Delaware often experiences a few tornadoes every year, this is only the second time the state has had tornado activity in November since 1950, according to the National Oceanic and Atmospheric Administration. The only other November tornado recorded was in 1989.</p><p>Severe storms have also resulted in tornadoes in Argentina as well as large hailstones. A round of severe thunderstorms moved through the central Córdoba province on Friday, bringing hailstones up to the size of a baseball (about 7.5cm in diameter). Parts of the province recorded up to 73mm of rainfall in just six hours early on Saturday. Such storms are common at this time of year. Water vapour from the Amazon meeting the Andes quickly condenses, resulting in massive cloud formations often associated with heavy downpours, lightning, tornadoes and large hailstones.</p> <a href="https://www.theguardian.com/environment/2026/nov/16/delaware-hit-by-rare-november-tornado">Continue reading...</a></description>

      <title>How Ukraine struck the Kerch bridge, a symbol of Putin’s rule</title>
      <link>https://www.theguardian.com/world/2026/nov/17/how-ukraine-struck-kerch-bridge-symbol-vladimir-putin-rule</link>
      <description><p>With the SpaceX satellite system faltering, Ukraine’s military launched a surprise, multi-pronged attack to take down vital bridge to Crimea</p><p>At 10pm on Monday evening a Ukrainian soldier scrawled a message on a kamikaze drone. It said simply: “The bridge is fucked.” He then added: “We will stand and Moscow will fall.” It was a freezing night, with a bright starry sky and no clouds. Lines of ice had formed on the drone’s bulky wings. Soon, it would be hurtling towards its target – about 500km to the south.</p><p>Typically the soldiers who gathered in this muddy field in central Ukraine were attacking oil refineries deep inside Russia. In recent months <a href="https://www.theguardian.com/news/ng-interactive/2026/aug/02/this-is-where-democracy-beats-totalitarianism-ukraines-drone-strike-force-takes-the-fight-to-russia">the work had become almost mundane:</a> they had hit so many of them. The objective that evening, however, was unique. It was a structure personally associated with Vladimir Putin and his grandiose imperial ambitions.</p> <a href="https://www.theguardian.com/world/2026/nov/17/how-ukraine-struck-kerch-bridge-symbol-vladimir-putin-rule">Continue reading...</a></description>

      <description><p>Partial demolition of bridge linking Russia and occupied Crimea is obvious embarrassment to Putin days before meeting with Xi and Trump</p><ul><li><p><a href="https://www.theguardian.com/world/live/2026/nov/17/europe-ukraine-russia-crimea-kerch-bridge-attack-latest-news-updates">Europe live – latest updates</a></p></li></ul><p>Ukraine’s attack on the Kerch road bridge overnight is the culmination of weeks, and perhaps months, of military operations plus years of industrial development, during which Kyiv has developed its own cruise missiles and long-range drones.</p><p>The demolition is not quite total, because the <a href="https://www.theguardian.com/world/2026/nov/17/ukraine-strikes-critical-damage-russia-kerch-bridge-crimea">rail bridge is still standing</a>, one line in operation – but the attack is an obvious embarrassment to Russia two days before Vladimir <a href="https://www.theguardian.com/world/2026/nov/16/xi-jinping-donald-trump-vladimir-putin-world-peace-trilateral-says-china">Putin is due to meet Donald Trump and Xi Jinping</a> in Shenzhen.</p> <a href="https://www.theguardian.com/world/2026/nov/17/ukraine-kerch-bridge-attack-russia-crimea-analysis">Continue reading...</a></description>

</description><media:thumbnail url="https://s.rfi.fr/media/display/29cb24b4-c8b7-11f1-9aa3-4dd8ac2cf3bf/w:1024/p:16x9/2026-10-15T145022Z-1497667603-RC2N3OANCMHS-RTRMADP-3-FRANCE-PROTEST.jpg"/><enclosure url="https://s.rfi.fr/media/display/29cb24b4-c8b7-11f1-9aa3-4dd8ac2cf3bf/w:1024/p:16x9/2026-10-15T145022Z-1497667603-RC2N3OANCMHS-RTRMADP-3-FRANCE-PROTEST.jpg" type="image/jpeg" length="0"/><guid isPermaLink="false">37288fa8-dcd4-11f1-aace-7ff548d44c0a</guid><pubDate>Tue, 10 Nov 2026 06:59:03 GMT</pubDate><source url="https://s.rfi.fr/media/display/29cb24b4-c8b7-11f1-9aa3-4dd8ac2cf3bf/w:1024/p:16x9/2026-10-15T145022Z-1497667603-RC2N3OANCMHS-RTRMADP-3-FRANCE-PROTEST.jpg">© Stephane Mahe/Reuters</source><dc:creator>RFI</dc:creator></item><item><category>France</category><title>Olympic judo champion Teddy Riner joins race for French presidency</title><link>https://www.rfi.fr/en/france/20261109-olympic-judo-champion-teddy-riner-joins-race-for-french-presidency</link><description>
France's five-time Olympic judo champion Teddy Riner announced on Monday that he would run in next year's presidential election, expressing concern particularly over "the rise of the far right".
</description><media:thumbnail url="https://s.rfi.fr/media/display/24e10c34-dc35-11f1-9eaf-695cb59fade5/w:1024/p:16x9/AP26313423095961.jpg"/><enclosure url="https://s.rfi.fr/media/display/24e10c34-dc35-11f1-9eaf-695cb59fade5/w:1024/p:16x9/AP26313423095961.jpg" type="image/jpeg" length="0"/><guid isPermaLink="false">ff9ac7be-dc3c-11f1-a6ee-d528d7ed3f40</guid><pubDate>Mon, 09 Nov 2026 17:44:42 GMT</pubDate><source url="https://s.rfi.fr/media/display/24e10c34-dc35-11f1-9eaf-695cb59fade5/w:1024/p:16x9/AP26313423095961.jpg">© AP - Michel Euler</source><dc:creator>RFI</dc:creator></item><item><category>France</category><title>French PM's move to increase minimum wage fails to convince unions</title><link>https://www.rfi.fr/en/france/20261109-french-pm-s-move-to-increase-minimum-wage-fails-to-convince-unions</link><description>
The French government on Monday announced a 1.6 percent increase in the national minimum wage, alongside a series of measures aimed at easing cost of living pressures. However, the decision fell well short of the demands of trade unions, who have called for fresh protests in the coming days.
</description><media:thumbnail url="https://s.rfi.fr/media/display/391ca27a-db78-11f1-86b0-d18c5759e759/w:1024/p:16x9/AP26311499885536.jpg"/><enclosure url="https://s.rfi.fr/media/display/391ca27a-db78-11f1-86b0-d18c5759e759/w:1024/p:16x9/AP26311499885536.jpg" type="image/jpeg" length="0"/><guid isPermaLink="false">1fb23d3e-dc42-11f1-9f6d-714e057b766f</guid><pubDate>Mon, 09 Nov 2026 17:36:17 GMT</pubDate><source url="https://s.rfi.fr/media/display/391ca27a-db78-11f1-86b0-d18c5759e759/w:1024/p:16x9/AP26311499885536.jpg">© Emma Da Silva/AP</source><dc:creator>RFI</dc:creator></item><item><category>France</category><title>'I still have nightmares': victim of police violence seeks justice six years on</title><link>https://www.rfi.fr/en/france/20261109-i-still-have-nightmares-victim-of-police-violence-seeks-justice-six-years-on-michel-zecler</link><description>
Three French police officers are due to go on trial on Monday over the brutal beating of black music producer Michel Zecler in Paris in 2020 – a case that sparked nationwide outrage over police violence and racism.
</description><media:thumbnail url="https://s.rfi.fr/media/display/88ce45b6-dba1-11f1-91d2-1beafce15fea/w:1024/p:16x9/FRANCE-JUSTICE-MICHEL-ZECLER.jpg"/><enclosure url="https://s.rfi.fr/media/display/88ce45b6-dba1-11f1-91d2-1beafce15fea/w:1024/p:16x9/FRANCE-JUSTICE-MICHEL-ZECLER.jpg" type="image/jpeg" length="0"/><guid isPermaLink="false">0aa97116-dc27-11f1-890c-17b2c492ee48</guid><pubDate>Mon, 09 Nov 2026 14:29:18 GMT</pubDate><source url="https://s.rfi.fr/media/display/88ce45b6-dba1-11f1-91d2-1beafce15fea/w:1024/p:16x9/FRANCE-JUSTICE-MICHEL-ZECLER.jpg">AFP - JOEL SAGET</source><dc:creator>RFI</dc:creator></item><item><category>France</category><title>Mélenchon bets on radical change as French presidential race takes shape</title><link>https://www.rfi.fr/en/france/20261109-m%C3%A9lenchon-bets-on-radical-change-as-french-presidential-race-takes-shape</link><description>
Leader of the hard-left France Unbowed party Jean-Luc Mélenchon has vowed to pursue an uncompromising programme of radical change, as he bids for the French presidency in 2027 – despite warnings that his divisive politics could ultimately hand victory to far-right National Rally leader Marine Le Pen.
</description><media:thumbnail url="https://s.rfi.fr/media/display/28b90688-dc1f-11f1-84be-bf1914cabd52/w:1024/p:16x9/M%C3%A9lenchon-7-November-2026.jpg"/><enclosure url="https://s.rfi.fr/media/display/28b90688-dc1f-11f1-84be-bf1914cabd52/w:1024/p:16x9/M%C3%A9lenchon-7-November-2026.jpg" type="image/jpeg" length="0"/><guid isPermaLink="false">273d195c-dc1a-11f1-8d60-5f29074843e0</guid><pubDate>Mon, 09 Nov 2026 13:01:32 GMT</pubDate><source url="https://s.rfi.fr/media/display/28b90688-dc1f-11f1-84be-bf1914cabd52/w:1024/p:16x9/M%C3%A9lenchon-7-November-2026.jpg">©  KENZO TRIBOUILLARD / AFP</source><dc:creator>RFI</dc:creator></item><item><category>France</category><title>French food bank donations fall as frequency of use spikes in cost of living crisis</title><link>https://www.rfi.fr/en/france/20261109-drop-in-french-food-bank-collection-as-rising-cost-of-living-hits-donations</link><description>
France’s annual food bank collection has gathered less than expected in the face of the rising cost of living, which has left people with less to spend on donations. The three-day campaign, which ended on Sunday, aimed to collect enough food to provide the equivalent of 20 million meals.
</description><media:thumbnail url="https://s.rfi.fr/media/display/b1392996-dbc2-11f1-af3e-bf1914cabd52/w:1024/p:16x9/000-32TL9GD-1.jpg"/><enclosure url="https://s.rfi.fr/media/display/b1392996-dbc2-11f1-af3e-bf1914cabd52/w:1024/p:16x9/000-32TL9GD-1.jpg" type="image/jpeg" length="0"/><guid isPermaLink="false">b7b3dffa-dc2b-11f1-8a7f-0f7ff0c2412a</guid><pubDate>Mon, 09 Nov 2026 12:09:22 GMT</pubDate><source url="https://s.rfi.fr/media/display/b1392996-dbc2-11f1-af3e-bf1914cabd52/w:1024/p:16x9/000-32TL9GD-1.jpg">© Mehdi Fedouach/AFP</source><dc:creator>RFI</dc:creator></item><item><category>France</category><title>French MPs weigh up debate on right-wing TV channel ban as petition tops 1m</title><link>https://www.rfi.fr/en/france/20261109-french-mps-to-weigh-debate-on-banning-conservative-tv-channel-as-petition-tops-1m-cnews</link><description>
A petition calling for French television channel CNews, often compared to American broadcaster Fox News, to be shut down has received more than a million signatures, two days before lawmakers meet to consider whether a ban should be debated in parliament.
</description><media:thumbnail url="https://s.rfi.fr/media/display/b0dc3b9c-dba8-11f1-b566-695cb59fade5/w:1024/p:16x9/000-D66Z6FA.jpg"/><enclosure url="https://s.rfi.fr/media/display/b0dc3b9c-dba8-11f1-b566-695cb59fade5/w:1024/p:16x9/000-D66Z6FA.jpg" type="image/jpeg" length="0"/><guid isPermaLink="false">19210fc8-dc0a-11f1-bd4e-25468b64d7d5</guid><pubDate>Mon, 09 Nov 2026 06:52:14 GMT</pubDate><source url="https://s.rfi.fr/media/display/b0dc3b9c-dba8-11f1-b566-695cb59fade5/w:1024/p:16x9/000-D66Z6FA.jpg">© Anne-Christine Poujoulat/AFP</source><dc:creator>RFI</dc:creator></item></channel></rss>

      <link>https://www.theguardian.com/football/2026/nov/17/wayne-rooney-contemplated-taking-own-life-during-playing-career-mental-health</link>
      <description><ul><li><p>Former England footballer opens up on mental health</p></li><li><p>‘It was probably the lowest point’ at Manchester United</p></li></ul><p>Wayne Rooney has revealed there was a period in his Manchester United career where he contemplated taking his own life. The former England striker said that, even as he flourished on the pitch, he was struggling with his mental health off it, despite being newly married and a dad to his eldest child, Kai.</p><p>He said he would spend two days at a time drinking at home and, he told the <a href="https://podcasts.apple.com/gb/podcast/wayne-rooney-growing-up-in-the-spotlight-fatherhood/id1527545442?i=1000802417716">Life At The Midpoint with Gabby Logan</a> podcast, at his lowest point considered taking his own life. “I can look back and say I was selfish, but I knew I was going through something which I was really struggling to deal with,” Rooney said. “Then I didn’t want Kai seeing me like that, so that’s why I’d hide away as well.</p> <a href="https://www.theguardian.com/football/2026/nov/17/wayne-rooney-contemplated-taking-own-life-during-playing-career-mental-health">Continue reading...</a></description>

      <title>Pocognoli’s aspiration for how Scotland must play is in danger of becoming unworkable</title>
      <link>https://www.theguardian.com/football/2026/nov/17/sebastien-pocognoli-scotland-nations-league-switzerland</link>
      <description><p>The 4-0 debacle against Switzerland has added to the tactical concerns about the head coach’s suitability, just six games into the job</p><p>The Scottish Football Association can only cling to a lesson from the past when assessing a worrying international window. Steve Clarke was beleaguered during his early games in charge. Successive 4-0 defeats by Belgium and Russia in 2019 left Clarke with the sense he should have stayed in club management. A revival meant Clarke led his country to three out of four tournaments.</p><p>There are, however, fundamental differences between the story of Clarke and that being delivered by Sébastien Pocognoli. Clarke was a pragmatist, whose decades in coaching suggested he had the wherewithal to revive Scotland. Pocognoli, six games into his tenure, is in danger of lurching in to the territory of dreamy ideologue whose aspiration for how Scotland must play is unworkable. The meek nature of Scotland’s collapse in the <a href="https://www.theguardian.com/football/2026/nov/16/switzerland-scotland-nations-league-match-report">4-0 loss to a second-string Switzerland</a> was lamentable. The Belgian’s assessment, with overpraise a key theme, raised eyebrows.</p> <a href="https://www.theguardian.com/football/2026/nov/17/sebastien-pocognoli-scotland-nations-league-switzerland">Continue reading...</a></description>

      <description><p><a href="https://www.theguardian.com/info/2022/nov/14/football-daily-email-sign-up"><strong>Sign up now! Sign up now! Sign up now? Sign up now!</strong></a></p><p>Barely six weeks ago, Jürgen Klopp’s big home debut in the Germany dugout ended in a deeply frustrating <a href="https://www.theguardian.com/football/2026/sep/27/nations-league-germany-greece-serbia-netherlands-norway-portugal">1-0 Nations League defeat to Greece</a> – but the manager tasked with returning <em>Die Mannschaft</em> to relevance claimed not to care. “I’m completely unbothered,” Klopp trilled unconvincingly. “I’ve lost far more matches than I would have liked, but as long as you draw the right conclusions, a loss is ultimately a piece of information – no different from a win.” It was a quote straight out of the Pierre Sage playbook for unfussed continental coaches – and probably worried a few German FA suits, given Klopp had already threatened to quit <em><a href="https://www.theguardian.com/football/2026/jul/24/germany-confirm-jurgen-klopp-new-head-coach">at his own unveiling</a></em> over potential media intrusion and criticism. “If you say tomorrow, ‘he’s [sh!t]’, tell me to my face and I’m out,” Klopp roared to <a href="https://www.theguardian.com/football/2026/jul/24/germany-confirm-jurgen-klopp-new-head-coach">trembling hacks in July</a>. That imagined confrontation now looks unlikely to take place, because his Germany side are suddenly very good indeed.</p> <a href="https://www.theguardian.com/football/2026/nov/17/jurgen-klopp-germany-project-football-daily-newsletter">Continue reading...</a></description>

      <title>Reliving the drama: England and Argentina stars watch 1986 classic with fresh eyes</title>
      <link>https://www.theguardian.com/football/2026/nov/17/reliving-the-drama-england-and-argentina-stars-watch-1986-classic-with-fresh-eyes</link>
      <description><p>A new film about the historic World Cup quarter-final clash finds new angles for a new generation</p><p>“Is there anything new to say about it?” Gary Lineker asked the producer Flora Fernandez-Marengo when she first approached him to take part in The Match, a documentary about the 1986 World Cup quarter-final between England and Argentina. Flora told an audience at the London film festival premiere of the film that she played her best card then and showed Lineker an image of Maradona with Queen in 1981, during the band’s tour of Argentina. Maradona wearing a union jack T-shirt and Freddie Mercury an Argentina strip. It worked. Lineker said yes.</p><p>The rock’n’roll angle, with Brian May as a talking head, is one of the very few details the film-makers added to Andrés Burgo’s book, The Match, on which the documentary is based. The directors Juan Cabral and Santiago Franco play with the timeline, hopping between past and present across 91 minutes, the exact duration of the match itself. Anecdotes that now form part of <a href="https://www.theguardian.com/football/2026/jul/14/diego-maradona-argentina-world-cup">Argentina’s football folklore</a> are spliced with excellent archive material.</p> <a href="https://www.theguardian.com/football/2026/nov/17/reliving-the-drama-england-and-argentina-stars-watch-1986-classic-with-fresh-eyes">Continue reading...</a></description>

      <link>https://www.theguardian.com/football/2026/nov/17/janine-van-wyck-south-africa-wafcon-book-extract-moving-the-goalposts-newsletter</link>
      <description><p>In an extract from the former South Africa captain’s book, she details less than ideal Wafcon 2006 preparations</p><p>I was just a year into my international career when we qualified for my first Wafcon, which was then called the African Women’s Championship (AWC) and was held in Nigeria in 2006. I was extremely excited but very nervous to participate in this tournament, more so when it was announced that we would be in the same group as the hosts, and would play them last in the group.</p><p>As it turned out, it would be the game that decided who finished top of the group. By then we had beaten Algeria 4-0 and Equatorial Guinea 2-0 and had to travel to Delta State to take on the hosts. I’d heard that Nigeria was the toughest country to travel to and I was about to realise why. It’s become common knowledge that South Africans and Nigerians are massive rivals on the football field but also don’t really get on off it.</p> <a href="https://www.theguardian.com/football/2026/nov/17/janine-van-wyck-south-africa-wafcon-book-extract-moving-the-goalposts-newsletter">Continue reading...</a></description>

      <title>Max Dowman shines in England colours and sends another record tumbling</title>
      <link>https://www.theguardian.com/football/2026/nov/17/max-dowman-england-under-21s-record-jude-bellingham</link>
      <description><p>Midfielder’s under-21s winner eclipsed Jude Bellingham’s mark and there was other talent to admire against France </p><p>There may have been an Mbappé on the pitch – Ethan, the younger brother of Kylian, with whom he shares a near-identical gait – but by the end there was only one precocious talent on the lips of those watching England overcome France in their under-21s clash. Max Dowman had done it again, lighting up another game, this time in filthy conditions at Ashton Gate. It was fitting he had the final say in a 3-2 win. The noise that accompanied his match-winning goal? Well, beyond the palpable excitement in the stands in Bristol, that would be the sound of the teenager sending yet another record tumbling.</p><p>Which one takes your fancy? Take your pick. At 14, playing for Arsenal Under-19s, he became the Uefa Youth League’s youngest goalscorer. This time last year, after taking to the field <a href="https://www.theguardian.com/football/2025/nov/04/slavia-prague-arsenal-champions-league-match-report">at Slavia Prague aged 15 and 308 days</a>, Dowman became the youngest player to feature in the Champions League. In March, six months on from his professional debut, he became the <a href="https://www.theguardian.com/football/2026/mar/14/arsenal-everton-premier-league-match-report">Premier League’s youngest goalscorer</a>. He is the youngest player to earn a Premier League winner’s medal. Last month he was presented with three Guinness World Records.</p> <a href="https://www.theguardian.com/football/2026/nov/17/max-dowman-england-under-21s-record-jude-bellingham">Continue reading...</a></description>

      <description><p>By supporting the non-profit BigShoe, the Arsenal forward has earned deserved plaudits for his social conscience</p><p>Valerie Fiesser will never forget her surprise when Bukayo Saka contacted her out of the blue in 2022, asking whether he could help support a project in Nigeria. “I remember thinking: ‘Is this really Bukayo writing us an email?’” says the president of BigShoe, a non-profit organisation based in Frankfurt that has helped more than 10,000 children worldwide. “But that’s how he is. He’s always asking what more we can do.”</p><p>Four years on from that unexpected email, Fiesser was given the secret task of reaching out for a letter for Saka to read from the podium when he was presented with the Sócrates award at <a href="https://www.theguardian.com/football/2026/oct/26/harry-kane-ends-englands-25-year-wait-for-a-mens-ballon-dor">last month’s Ballon d’Or ceremony in London</a> for his humanitarian work. She got the words from Byiringiro, a 14-year-old from Rwanda who had his eyesight restored after having surgery thanks to a BigShoe initiative.</p> <a href="https://www.theguardian.com/football/2026/nov/17/he-wants-to-change-lives-the-story-behind-bukayo-sakas-socrates-award">Continue reading...</a></description>

      <description><ul><li><p>Deal will run to 2031 and worth about £300,000 a week</p></li><li><p>Jurriën Timber also agrees fresh contract extension</p></li></ul><p>Declan Rice has agreed a new five-year contract at Arsenal, with the England midfielder poised to match Bukayo Saka’s status as the highest-paid player at the Premier League champions.</p><p>Representatives for Rice, who won his 82nd cap in <a href="https://www.theguardian.com/football/2026/nov/15/spain-england-nations-league-match-report">England’s thrilling win over Spain</a> on Sunday, have been in talks for months about extending the deal he signed in 2023 after a record £105m move from West Ham. That is believed to be worth about £250,000 a week and is due to expire in 2028, although Arsenal have the option of a further 12 months.</p> <a href="https://www.theguardian.com/football/2026/nov/17/declan-rice-new-arsenal-contract-jurrien-timber">Continue reading...</a></description>

      <title>Fifa accused of climate ‘record of failure’ due to Aramco deal and tournament expansion</title>
      <link>https://www.theguardian.com/football/2026/nov/17/fifa-accused-climate-record-failure-aramco-deal-tournament-expansion</link>
      <description><ul><li><p>Groups question ‘sincerity’ to meet emissions pledges</p></li><li><p>Oil giant is a major sponsor of football governing body</p></li></ul><p>The United Nations has been asked to review Fifa’s status as a signatory to a key environmental initiative, with complainants arguing football’s governing body has a “record of failure” on climate action.</p><p>Fifa <a href="https://inside.fifa.com/sustainability/news/fifa-joins-the-un-sports-for-climate-action-framework">is a signatory</a> to the UN’s Sports for Climate Action Framework, a coalition which seeks to persuade sporting organisations to “work together to achieve a climate-resilient future”. Under the framework, signatories agree to cut their greenhouse gas emissions by 50% by 2030 and to “partner with key stakeholders to deliver joint climate action”. They can have their status as a signatory removed, however, if “sincerity in participation or ability to participate is a cause for concern”.</p> <a href="https://www.theguardian.com/football/2026/nov/17/fifa-accused-climate-record-failure-aramco-deal-tournament-expansion">Continue reading...</a></description>

      <description><p>A match that should have been about 103 was instead about four. Scottish FA giddiness about Pocognoli as the successor to Steve Clarke, a hugely successful leader of the national team, is looking increasingly ridiculous. “I don’t think you’ve got time in international football,” said Robertson as dust settled here.       <title>Echoes of Azteca but not like Argentina: fearless England start afresh in Madrid</title>
      <link>https://www.theguardian.com/football/2026/nov/17/azteca-argentina-fearless-england-start-afresh-spain</link>
      <description><p>‘We will not go back on this way of playing,’ says Thomas Tuchel after he delivered response to World Cup critics</p><p>Thomas Tuchel made defensive substitutions as England protected a lead. He finished with three centre-backs on the pitch. His team could not get out of their half in the final part of the game. So close your eyes and imagine an alternate universe in which James Trafford did not make his stunning double save in stoppage time on Sunday and England had drawn 3-3 with Spain at the Metropolitano Stadium rather than <a href="https://www.theguardian.com/football/2026/nov/15/spain-england-nations-league-match-report">won 3-2</a>. The reaction would not have been kind because Tuchel has been here before.</p><p>The head coach wanted to push one particular comparison from the World Cup over the summer. “It was Mexico reloaded,” he said, with a nod towards the 3-2 last-16 <a href="https://www.theguardian.com/football/2026/jul/06/england-mexico-match-report-jude-bellingham-harry-kane-world-cup">win at the Azteca Stadium</a> and it fitted like a glove – down to the detail of Jarell Quansah and red cards.</p> <a href="https://www.theguardian.com/football/2026/nov/17/azteca-argentina-fearless-england-start-afresh-spain">Continue reading...</a></description>

      <title>Danny Kelly obituary</title>
      <link>https://www.theguardian.com/media/2026/nov/17/danny-kelly-obituary</link>
      <description><p>Ebullient journalist, magazine editor and broadcaster whose passion for music and football shone through all his work</p><p>Danny Kelly, who has died aged 69, influenced music journalism and sports broadcasting for more than four decades. Humour, enthusiasm and encyclopedic knowledge were the hallmarks of his work as a writer and editor at the New Musical Express (NME) and Q magazine, and throughout his online, TV and audio career, most prominently around his passion for football.</p><p>In 1997 Kelly helped set up Football 365, one of the earliest football websites, and still one of the most popular in the UK. He hosted radio shows on BBC 5 Live, TalkSport, BT Sport and Times Radio, as well as many podcasts including The View from the Lane, about the team he had supported since childhood, Tottenham Hotspur.</p> <a href="https://www.theguardian.com/media/2026/nov/17/danny-kelly-obituary">Continue reading...</a></description>

      <link>https://www.theguardian.com/football/2026/nov/17/thomas-frank-crystal-palace-pierre-sage-sacked-steve-parish</link>
      <description><p>Seeking redemption after failing at Spurs, newly installed Crystal Palace manager has a tough challenge ahead</p><p>Thomas Frank promised his wife, Nanna, he would take a year’s sabbatical <a href="https://www.theguardian.com/football/2026/feb/11/tottenhams-soaring-dreams-for-thomas-frank-quickly-hit-the-buffers-of-grim-reality">after being sacked by Tottenham in February</a>, but he couldn’t wait that long. Having received a reported £8m payoff from Spurs, he kept an extremely low profile in the first few months after an experience at the club that sources close to the 53‑year‑old have described as “traumatic”.</p><p>Frank broke his silence at the start of June with a statement released by the League Managers Association. It said he would cover the World Cup for the BBC (thereby going head-to-head with Ange Postecoglou, his predecessor at Spurs, who worked for ITV) before “experiencing the Tour de France”, a lifelong passion. Frank usually preferred to run to Brentford’s training ground and home matches from his home in East Sheen during a nine‑year spell as assistant and then manager, but he occasionally cycled because it helped to clear his head.</p> <a href="https://www.theguardian.com/football/2026/nov/17/thomas-frank-crystal-palace-pierre-sage-sacked-steve-parish">Continue reading...</a></description>

      <title>WSL talking points: Chelsea’s gamble pays off and have Arsenal lost fear factor?</title>
      <link>https://www.theguardian.com/football/2026/nov/16/wsl-talking-points-chelseas-gamble-pays-off-and-have-arsenal-lost-fear-factor</link>
      <description><p>Blues beat champions after bold substitution and Gunners’ home struggles continue with fifth consecutive WSL draw</p><p>Sonia Bompastor attempted to deflect suggestions that the removal of Kadeisha Buchanan 12 minutes into Chelsea’s top-of-the-table clash with Manchester City was tactical, but few were convinced by the claim that it was down to injury. The manager said the centre-back, who had not asked to come off and walked straight down the tunnel, had taken a knock to the head in training and been assessed and cleared, but that during the game “she was not herself”. On came Veerle Buurman and the threat of Khadija Shaw was nullified, the Dutch defender restricting the golden boot favourite so well that Shaw did not manage a shot on target. Bompastor said after the game that she had not spoken to Buchanan but that she would “explain myself to her”. “I always have good relationships with the players, bring them clarity, and I’m always direct and honest so they have the information,” she said. “It won’t be any different.” Enforced or not, the substitution was a huge gamble that paid off, even after the loss of Melvine Malard to injury in the first half reduced their number of remaining in-game substitution windows to one. <strong>Suzanne Wrack</strong></p><p><em><a href="https://www.theguardian.com/football/2026/nov/14/chelsea-manchester-city-womens-super-league-match-report">Match report: Chelsea 1-0 Manchester City</a></em></p> <a href="https://www.theguardian.com/football/2026/nov/16/wsl-talking-points-chelseas-gamble-pays-off-and-have-arsenal-lost-fear-factor">Continue reading...</a></description>

      <title>Pochettino: I’d tell Guardiola to ‘take it’ if he’s offered US coaching job</title>
      <link>https://www.theguardian.com/football/2026/nov/16/mauricio-pochettino-pep-guardiola-usmnt-manchester-united</link>
      <description><p>As he prepares to depart for Manchester United, the outgoing US coach held court on a number of topics, including what he’d change about soccer in America</p><p>Outgoing US head coach Mauricio Pochettino and former Manchester City head coach Pep Guardiola have a long, storied past. The two faced each other as players, when Guardiola was at Barcelona and Pochettino was making his name across town at Espanyol. They faced each other 22 times as managers in the Premier League and the two share a mutual respect – and intensity – when it comes to their approach to playing and coaching alike.</p><p>So when Guardiola visited Yankee Stadium in September to serve as New York City FC’s pre-match hype man before their rivalry match with Red Bull New York, Pochettino – in town anyways to scout the match – made it a point to sit with him during the game. He brought along his assistant coach and confidant Jesús Pérez, and US Soccer CEO and secretary general JT Batson.</p> <a href="https://www.theguardian.com/football/2026/nov/16/mauricio-pochettino-pep-guardiola-usmnt-manchester-united">Continue reading...</a></description>

      <description><p>International investigation using trove of leaked internal data allegedly shows German bank overlooked compliance concerns to safeguard profits</p><p>Deutsche Bank reportedly dismissed warnings about its dealings with risky clients, including high-profile Russian oligarchs, to protect profits, the findings of an investigation into a trove of leaked bank documents indicate.</p><p>A leak of 15m internal files is reported to show that the troubled German bank repeatedly ignored concerns by its compliance officers about its risk-taking, despite having already <a href="https://www.theguardian.com/business/2019/apr/17/deutsche-bank-faces-action-over-20bn-russian-money-laundering-scheme">been caught being used to launder billions of dollars</a> for Russian criminals, spies and oligarchs between 2010 and 2015.</p> <a href="https://www.theguardian.com/business/2026/nov/17/deutsche-bank-dimissed-warnings-risky-clients-reports-claim">Continue reading...</a></description>

      <link>https://www.theguardian.com/business/live/2026/nov/17/uk-jobs-market-wage-growth-payrolls-unemployment-milburn-china-us-chips-latest-news-updates</link>
      <description><p>Rolling coverage of the latest economic and financial news</p><ul><li><p><a href="https://www.theguardian.com/technology/2026/nov/17/nvidia-jensen-huang-statement"><strong>Jensen Huang says he would be ‘honored’ to return to Nvidia as CEO</strong></a></p></li><li><p><a href="https://www.theguardian.com/global/2026/nov/16/jensen-huang-nvidia-ceo-china"><strong>Jensen Huang’s departure as Nvidia CEO becomes a political proxy war</strong></a></p></li></ul><p><strong>China has threatened to retaliate against the US after Washington tightened restrictions on remote access to AI chips and servers.</strong></p><p>At a press conference on Tuesday, China’s foreign ministry spokesperson <strong>Guo</strong> <strong>Jiakun</strong> said Beijing would take “necessary measures” to safeguard its own interests, saying:</p><p>“The US has repeatedly overstretched the concept of national security, abused export controls and even interfered in China’s normal trade and technological cooperation with other countries, unjustifiably suppressing the development of China’s high-tech industries.”</p><p>“This is the worst situation possible for China because the last thing they want to see is any new restrictions on their access to chips.”</p><p>“Export controls are what upset them practically more than anything else right now other than maybe Taiwan.”</p><p>Deutsche plotted an expansion of its <a href="https://www.ft.com/content/bf775dda-4148-49f9-a8b4-a4a02f44207e">notorious Russia business</a> under chief executive Christian Sewing, over-ruling the fears of its compliance team about the bank’s Kremlin-connected clientele as geopolitical storm clouds gathered.</p><p>The bank <a href="https://www.ft.com/content/784cbdc7-c852-4081-b1e5-390779e9fad1">accidentally leaked Trump’s tax statements</a> during his first presidential term and kept the mistake secret from the White House, with Sewing briefed on its handling of the crisis.</p><p>Deutsche processed almost $600mn of suspicious <a href="https://www.ft.com/content/72ac6fee-55f3-4db5-a1e3-873ef39c0b96">payments linked to Jeffrey Epstein</a>, a far higher figure than previously known.</p><p>A <a href="https://www.ft.com/content/4f8dae68-bfec-43bd-bef6-b830815ec538">catalogue</a> of compliance deficiencies, governance weaknesses, ineptitude and technology failings, including a confession to regulators that Deutsche was in effect “operating outside of law and order”.</p> <a href="https://www.theguardian.com/business/live/2026/nov/17/uk-jobs-market-wage-growth-payrolls-unemployment-milburn-china-us-chips-latest-news-updates">Continue reading...</a></description>

      <title>Farewell to Elon Musk’s Cybertruck. Has any car ever been more repellent? | Arwa Mahdawi</title>
      <link>https://www.theguardian.com/commentisfree/2026/nov/11/farewell-cybertruck-elon-musk-car-repellent</link>
      <description><p>Safety campaigners have condemned it and owners have complained about it. Goodbye to a steel monstrosity seemingly designed by a five-year-old</p><p>Elon Musk is having a rough go of it, isn’t he? The world’s richest man spent almost half a billion dollars on the <a href="https://www.theguardian.com/technology/2026/nov/04/elon-musk-midterm-spending-analysis">midterms</a> in a failed attempt to defend Republican control of government. Now the tech mogul, who moved from California to Texas to escape Democrats and regulations, finds himself in a newly blue state. He also finds himself the subject of an unflattering <a href="https://www.theguardian.com/film/2026/sep/08/musk-review-epic-study-worlds-richest-most-banal-man-elon-film">documentary</a> and, if the Democrats follow through on threats to investigate him, could potentially be in a spot of legal bother.</p><p>And to top it all off? Musk’s beloved Cybertruck, the steel monstrosity that looks as if it were designed by a five-year-old, is <a href="https://www.theguardian.com/technology/2026/nov/06/tesla-to-wind-down-cybertruck-production-as-elon-musk-focuses-on-robotics-and-ai">winding down production</a>. According to Musk, this isn’t because it’s an abject failure, but because he is channelling his energy into other things. “This is not a case of Cybertruck being unprofitable, as has been misreported by legacy media,” Musk <a href="https://x.com/elonmusk/status/2119691615774146614?a=pN3ISFVZZ-aU4_-TlJw&amp;s=20">tweeted</a> on Monday. “But rather that the opportunity cost of the complexity of Cybertruck is vastly outweighed by the value of incremental Cybercab production.” (The Cybercab is a two-passenger robotaxi.)</p> <a href="https://www.theguardian.com/commentisfree/2026/nov/11/farewell-cybertruck-elon-musk-car-repellent">Continue reading...</a></description>

      <description><p>Company insists Alice Huang, who is accused of being a Chinese spy, left business in late 2025</p><ul><li><p><a href="https://www.theguardian.com/technology/2026/nov/16/elon-musk-tech-execs-open-letter-jensen-huang-return-nvidia-ceo">Elon Musk joins 165,000 others calling for Nvidia to bring back Jensen Huang</a></p></li><li><p><a href="https://www.theguardian.com/business/live/2026/nov/16/ai-sell-off-resumes-jensen-huang-discusses-comeback-nvidia-ceo-dollar-stock-markets-latest-news-updates">Business live – latest updates</a></p></li></ul><p>Megaspeed International, the company linked to the downfall of the Nvidia chief, <a href="https://www.theguardian.com/technology/jensen-huang">Jensen Huang</a>, says it is a “legitimate and lawful business” and has announced that its director, who allegedly had an affair with Jensen Huang, left the business in late 2025.</p><p>The Singapore-based cloud computing company on the weekend said it was “aware of recent media reports containing assertions about our business, supply chain and global operations that are not supported by verifiable evidence”.</p> <a href="https://www.theguardian.com/technology/2026/nov/16/megaspeed-company-breaks-slience-nvidia-jensen-huang-alice-huang">Continue reading...</a></description>

La candidate du Rassemblement national à l’élection présidentielle de 2027, Marine Le Pen, a présenté mardi son projet de réforme du système de retraites, avec la promesse d'un retour aux 62 ans, voire 60 ans, financé par davantage de travail et une dose de capitalisation obligatoire. À cinq mois du premier tour de l'élection présidentielle en France, la droite cherche son candidat pour "éviter la dispersion des voix", selon Gabriel Attal. La question d'une primaire de droite se pose alors, bien qu'Édouard Philippe refuse catégoriquement d'y prendre part pour l'instant. Les précisions de Fleur Simon, chroniqueuse politique à France 24.
</description><media:thumbnail url="https://s.france24.com/media/display/af02a3ac-e1b5-11f1-ac84-29048b396e03/w:1024/p:16x9/FR-20261116-110525-111039-CS-01.jpg"/><enclosure url="https://s.france24.com/media/display/af02a3ac-e1b5-11f1-ac84-29048b396e03/w:1024/p:16x9/FR-20261116-110525-111039-CS-01.jpg" type="image/jpeg" length="0"/><guid isPermaLink="false">b5c9f41a-e1b5-11f1-928f-8f345d858e2a</guid><pubDate>Mon, 16 Nov 2026 13:33:09 GMT</pubDate><dc:creator>FRANCE24</dc:creator></item><item><category></category><title>France : le lycée Neslon Mandela rouvre ses portes à Nantes</title><link>https://www.france24.com/fr/vid%C3%A9o/20261116-france-le-lyc%C3%A9e-neslon-mandela-rouvre-ses-portes-%C3%A0-nantes</link><description>
Le lycée Nelson-Mandela de Nantes, en partie incendié début octobre en marge de la mobilisation lycéenne, a rouvert ses portes lundi 16 novembre au matin pour une reprise partielle des cours, tandis que les travaux se poursuivent sur la partie des bâtiments encore endommagée. Le ministre de l'Éducation, Édouard Geffray, venu pour la réouverture des portes du lycée, a été hué par des élèves lors de son arrivée, ces derniers étant consternés par le manque d'écoute de leurs revendications.
</description><media:thumbnail url="https://s.france24.com/media/display/4c6b2b04-e1ad-11f1-b22c-29048b396e03/w:1024/p:16x9/FR-20261116-110349-110453-CS-01.jpg"/><enclosure url="https://s.france24.com/media/display/4c6b2b04-e1ad-11f1-b22c-29048b396e03/w:1024/p:16x9/FR-20261116-110349-110453-CS-01.jpg" type="image/jpeg" length="0"/><guid isPermaLink="false">52960e5e-e1ad-11f1-a68b-e72ad7e160a9</guid><pubDate>Mon, 16 Nov 2026 11:33:00 GMT</pubDate><dc:creator>FRANCE24</dc:creator></item><item><category></category><title>Sommet de l'OIF : la Francophonie c'est quoi ?</title><link>https://www.france24.com/fr/vid%C3%A9o/20261116-sommet-de-l-oif-la-francophonie-c-est-quoi</link><description>
Le sommet de l'Organisation internationale de la Francophonie (OIF) prend place tous les deux ans. L'objectif principal : promouvoir la langue française et son apprentissage. Les chefs d'État et de gouvernement des 90 membres de l'organisation, parmi lesquels le président français et le Premier ministre canadien Mark Carney, sont donc réunis depuis le 15 novembre jusqu'à ce lundi 16 au soir, à Phnom Penh, au Cambodge.
</description><media:thumbnail url="https://s.france24.com/media/display/0d38e954-e1a2-11f1-bef8-3f371022a770/w:1024/p:16x9/FR-20261116-090611-090759-CS.jpg"/><enclosure url="https://s.france24.com/media/display/0d38e954-e1a2-11f1-bef8-3f371022a770/w:1024/p:16x9/FR-20261116-090611-090759-CS.jpg" type="image/jpeg" length="0"/><guid isPermaLink="false">13d252f0-e1a2-11f1-898d-fd8ff3c4ca96</guid><pubDate>Mon, 16 Nov 2026 10:32:27 GMT</pubDate><dc:creator>FRANCE24</dc:creator></item><item><category>France</category><title>Depardieu se désiste de son procès en appel pour agressions sexuelles et présente ses "excuses"</title><link>https://www.france24.com/fr/france/20261116-g%C3%A9rard-depardieu-se-d%C3%A9siste-proc%C3%A8s-appel-agressions-sexuelles-pr%C3%A9sente-excuses</link><description>
Dans un communiqué intitulé "J'entends" et publié lundi, Gérard Depardieu a annoncé "assumer" sa condamnation à 18 mois de prison avec sursis prononcée en mai 2025 pour deux agressions sexuelles commises sur le tournage d'un film. L'acteur présente également des "excuses, profondes et sincères", à celles et ceux qui ont "pu en souffrir".
</description><media:thumbnail url="https://s.france24.com/media/display/27b9d0d2-0994-11f0-8616-005056bfb2b6/w:1024/p:16x9/2025-03-25T130552Z_2141627969_RC2BKDAVMBUK_RTRMADP_3_PEOPLE-DEPARDIEU-TRIAL.JPG"/><enclosure url="https://s.france24.com/media/display/27b9d0d2-0994-11f0-8616-005056bfb2b6/w:1024/p:16x9/2025-03-25T130552Z_2141627969_RC2BKDAVMBUK_RTRMADP_3_PEOPLE-DEPARDIEU-TRIAL.JPG" type="image/jpeg" length="0"/><guid isPermaLink="false">c7498a90-e19f-11f1-87a6-5b70f60db3bf</guid><pubDate>Mon, 16 Nov 2026 10:11:54 GMT</pubDate><source url="https://s.france24.com/media/display/27b9d0d2-0994-11f0-8616-005056bfb2b6/w:1024/p:16x9/2025-03-25T130552Z_2141627969_RC2BKDAVMBUK_RTRMADP_3_PEOPLE-DEPARDIEU-TRIAL.JPG">© Stéphanie Lecocq, Reuters</source><dc:creator>FRANCE 24</dc:creator></item><item><category>France</category><title>Francophonie : l'élection du secrétaire général reportée, Macron salue un "compromis"</title><link>https://www.france24.com/fr/france/20261116-francophonie-oif-vote-%C3%A9lection-secr%C3%A9taire-g%C3%A9n%C3%A9ral-louise-mushikiwabo-rwanda-rd-congo-juliana-lumumba-dacian-ciolos-coumba-ba</link><description>
L'élection du secrétaire général de l'Organisation internationale de la Francophonie a été reportée d'un an lundi à Phnom Penh, au Cambodge. Après deux mandats de Louise Mushikiwabo, la République démocratique du Congo, qui accuse le Rwanda de soutenir le groupe armé rebelle du M23 dans ses provinces de l'Est, s'opposait à une reconduction de la Rwandaise à la tête de l'OIF. Emmanuel Macron a salué un "compromis" à l'issue du vote.
</description><media:thumbnail url="https://s.france24.com/media/display/68751798-e198-11f1-942f-f71d22e7fea9/w:1024/p:16x9/000-D7KK3BH.jpg"/><enclosure url="https://s.france24.com/media/display/68751798-e198-11f1-942f-f71d22e7fea9/w:1024/p:16x9/000-D7KK3BH.jpg" type="image/jpeg" length="0"/><guid isPermaLink="false">c9b8fab2-e187-11f1-858f-1b42b7e5011f</guid><pubDate>Mon, 16 Nov 2026 07:01:33 GMT</pubDate><source url="https://s.france24.com/media/display/68751798-e198-11f1-942f-f71d22e7fea9/w:1024/p:16x9/000-D7KK3BH.jpg">© Anthony Wallace, AFP</source><dc:creator>FRANCE 24</dc:creator></item><item><category>France</category><title>Les rassemblements autour de certains lycées et universités interdits à Paris</title><link>https://www.france24.com/fr/france/20261115-les-rassemblements-autour-de-certains-lyc%C3%A9es-et-universit%C3%A9s-interdits-%C3%A0-paris</link><description>
Publié dimanche, un arrêté préfectoral prévoit l'interdiction de tout rassemblement ou cortège non déclaré "dans un rayon de 100 mètres" autour de dix lycées et cinq sites universitaires de Paris. Le syndicat étudiant Unef a exigé son "retrait immédiat" et annoncé saisir le tribunal administratif en référé.
</description><media:thumbnail url="https://s.france24.com/media/display/db2fef7c-e131-11f1-9207-3f371022a770/w:1024/p:16x9/f0aeab414202f2310983b4484d8d480e292a891c.jpg"/><enclosure url="https://s.france24.com/media/display/db2fef7c-e131-11f1-9207-3f371022a770/w:1024/p:16x9/f0aeab414202f2310983b4484d8d480e292a891c.jpg" type="image/jpeg" length="0"/><guid isPermaLink="false">dbbdebba-e131-11f1-b374-e11b42a11ff8</guid><pubDate>Sun, 15 Nov 2026 20:19:27 GMT</pubDate><source url="https://s.france24.com/media/display/db2fef7c-e131-11f1-9207-3f371022a770/w:1024/p:16x9/f0aeab414202f2310983b4484d8d480e292a891c.jpg">© Mehdi Fedouach, AFP</source><dc:creator>FRANCE 24</dc:creator></item><item><category>France</category><title>Présidentielle 2027 : Teddy Riner affronte son premier sondage, David Lisnard gagne des points</title><link>https://www.france24.com/fr/france/20261115-pr%C3%A9sidentielle-2027-teddy-riner-cr%C3%A9dit%C3%A9-de-4-5-dans-un-sondage-david-lisnard-gagne-des-points</link><description>
Le candidat tout juste déclaré Teddy Riner est crédité de 4,5 % des intentions de vote dans un sondage pour BFMTV et La Tribune Dimanche. Selon cette enquête, le maire de Cannes, David Lisnard, fait un bon de quatre points au détriment de Bruno Retailleau. Marine Le Pen reste en tête des intentions de vote, suivie par Jean-Luc Mélenchon, qui s'installe à la deuxième place. 
</description><media:thumbnail url="https://s.france24.com/media/display/af92d8aa-e0d4-11f1-a352-5f54d898a954/w:1024/p:16x9/000-C6WN7K6.jpg"/><enclosure url="https://s.france24.com/media/display/af92d8aa-e0d4-11f1-a352-5f54d898a954/w:1024/p:16x9/000-C6WN7K6.jpg" type="image/jpeg" length="0"/><guid isPermaLink="false">480c5ff2-e0d5-11f1-b132-ad05df6f53f9</guid><pubDate>Sun, 15 Nov 2026 09:35:16 GMT</pubDate><source url="https://s.france24.com/media/display/af92d8aa-e0d4-11f1-a352-5f54d898a954/w:1024/p:16x9/000-C6WN7K6.jpg">© Valery Hache, AFP</source><dc:creator>FRANCE 24</dc:creator></item><item><category>France</category><title>Acte V du mouvement social : des revendications variées, une affluence en baisse</title><link>https://www.france24.com/fr/france/20261114-acte-v-du-mouvement-social-des-revendications-vari%C3%A9es-une-affluence-en-baisse</link><description>
Lors de l'acte V du mouvement social qui ébranle la France, quelque 106 000 à 200 000 personnes ont défilé samedi dans toute la France, selon les chiffres du ministère de l'Intérieur et l'intersyndicale jeune (Union étudiane, USL, Fage, Unef). Quelques incidents se sont produits et des journalistes ont été agressés. 
</description><media:thumbnail url="https://s.france24.com/media/display/a840c416-e072-11f1-b800-f71d22e7fea9/w:1024/p:16x9/2026-11-14T161721Z-1217346689-RC2SNOASVFNM-RTRMADP-3-FRANCE-PROTEST.jpg"/><enclosure url="https://s.france24.com/media/display/a840c416-e072-11f1-b800-f71d22e7fea9/w:1024/p:16x9/2026-11-14T161721Z-1217346689-RC2SNOASVFNM-RTRMADP-3-FRANCE-PROTEST.jpg" type="image/jpeg" length="0"/><guid isPermaLink="false">69216d38-e074-11f1-9636-49d8787f523b</guid><pubDate>Sat, 14 Nov 2026 21:43:20 GMT</pubDate><source url="https://s.france24.com/media/display/a840c416-e072-11f1-b800-f71d22e7fea9/w:1024/p:16x9/2026-11-14T161721Z-1217346689-RC2SNOASVFNM-RTRMADP-3-FRANCE-PROTEST.jpg">©  Benoit Tessier, Reuters</source><dc:creator>FRANCE 24</dc:creator></item></channel></rss>

<rss version="2.0" xmlns:atom="http://www.w3.org/2005/Atom" xmlns:media="http://search.yahoo.com/mrss/" xmlns:dc="http://purl.org/dc/elements/1.1/"><channel><language>fr</language><title>L'actualité économique et politique en Europe - RFI</title><description>Suivez l'actualité en direct dédiée au continent Européen - Les derniers reportages, news et informations en continu en Europe, Emissions, Podcast, dossiers sur RFI.</description><link>https://www.rfi.fr/fr/europe/</link><lastBuildDate>Tue, 17 Nov 2026 17:31:26 GMT</lastBuildDate><atom:link href="https://www.rfi.fr/fr/europe/rss" rel="self" type="application/rss+xml"/><item><category>Europe</category><title>Allemagne: la Deutsche Bank au cœur d'un nouveau scandale de pratiques douteuses</title><link>https://www.rfi.fr/fr/europe/20261117-allemagne-la-deutsche-bank-au-c%C5%93ur-d-un-nouveau-scandale-de-pratiques-douteuses</link><description>
La plus grande institution bancaire allemande fait une nouvelle fois la une de la presse, mardi 17 novembre 2026. Une fuite de 15 millions de documents lève le voile sur ses pratiques douteuses et la manière dont la Deutsche Bank a protégé ses clients les plus sulfureux, comme le pédocriminel américain Jeffrey Epstein.
</description><media:thumbnail url="https://s.rfi.fr/media/display/bf6972a8-e2a4-11f1-8961-7908c4e1a3c7/w:1024/p:16x9/ALLEMAGNE-BERLIN-DEUTSCHE-BANK.jpg"/><enclosure url="https://s.rfi.fr/media/display/bf6972a8-e2a4-11f1-8961-7908c4e1a3c7/w:1024/p:16x9/ALLEMAGNE-BERLIN-DEUTSCHE-BANK.jpg" type="image/jpeg" length="0"/><guid isPermaLink="false">d113dcd2-e2a4-11f1-9635-7d42f883cc1b</guid><pubDate>Tue, 17 Nov 2026 16:35:05 GMT</pubDate><source url="https://s.rfi.fr/media/display/bf6972a8-e2a4-11f1-8961-7908c4e1a3c7/w:1024/p:16x9/ALLEMAGNE-BERLIN-DEUTSCHE-BANK.jpg">REUTERS - Nadja Wohlleben</source><dc:creator>Nathanaël Vittrant</dc:creator></item><item><category>Invité international</category><title>Projet de «hub de retour»: «On n'a aucune idée de la manière dont le Rwanda va traiter ces étrangers»</title><link>https://www.rfi.fr/fr/podcasts/invit%C3%A9-international/20261117-projet-de-hub-de-retour-on-n-a-aucune-id%C3%A9e-de-la-mani%C3%A8re-dont-le-rwanda-va-traiter-ces-%C3%A9trangers</link><description>
« Ni avenir, ni humanité dans le projet de centre de migrants au Rwanda » : ce sont les mots du Premier ministre espagnol, Pedro Sanchez, face à l'initiative détaillée, lundi 16 novembre, par cinq pays de l'Union européenne, dont l'Allemagne et le Danemark, d'ouvrir dans ce pays le tout premier centre pour des migrants expulsés d'Europe. Les promoteurs du projet assurent vouloir créer un centre ouvert, où les migrants seront accompagnés et pourront bénéficier de programmes de formation, d'accès à l’emploi, ainsi qu'à l'éducation et à des centres de santé. Assiste-t-on à un tournant dans le durcissement de l'Europe en matière d'immigration ? L'analyse d'Antoine Pecoud, professeur de sociologie à l'université de Sorbonne Paris-Nord et directeur du département Policy de l'Institut des migrations. 
</description><media:thumbnail url="https://s.rfi.fr/media/display/4f886fa4-a8eb-11f1-80af-005056bf30b7/w:1024/p:16x9/2026-09-04T160250Z-834668253-RC2CCNAR7GC0-RTRMADP-3-EU-IMMIGRATION.jpg"/><enclosure url="https://s.rfi.fr/media/display/4f886fa4-a8eb-11f1-80af-005056bf30b7/w:1024/p:16x9/2026-09-04T160250Z-834668253-RC2CCNAR7GC0-RTRMADP-3-EU-IMMIGRATION.jpg" type="image/jpeg" length="0"/><guid isPermaLink="false">21af5d90-e27f-11f1-8e59-9ff547092806</guid><pubDate>Tue, 17 Nov 2026 15:02:50 GMT</pubDate><dc:creator>Candice Mazaud-Tomazic</dc:creator></item><item><category>Europe</category><title>Comment l’Ukraine a en partie détruit le pont de Kertch en Crimée</title><link>https://www.rfi.fr/fr/europe/20261117-comment-l-ukraine-a-en-partie-d%C3%A9truit-le-pont-de-kertch</link><description>
Cible prioritaire de l’Ukraine depuis le début de l’invasion russe, le pont de Kertch reliant la Crimée à la Russie n’est plus utilisable. Après de premières frappes lundi 16 novembre, l’armée ukrainienne a de nouveau ciblé cet ouvrage à la fois stratégique et symbolique ce mardi. Les images disponibles en sources ouvertes montrent qu’une partie importante de la section routière a été détruite.
</description><media:thumbnail url="https://s.rfi.fr/media/display/6de17860-e284-11f1-adba-6d75ed565170/w:1024/p:16x9/Russie-Ukraine-Kertch-Info-Verif-Une.png"/><enclosure url="https://s.rfi.fr/media/display/6de17860-e284-11f1-adba-6d75ed565170/w:1024/p:16x9/Russie-Ukraine-Kertch-Info-Verif-Une.png" type="image/png" length="0"/><guid isPermaLink="false">efa87d34-e285-11f1-8673-6541d1e7a339</guid><pubDate>Tue, 17 Nov 2026 13:11:05 GMT</pubDate><source url="https://s.rfi.fr/media/display/6de17860-e284-11f1-adba-6d75ed565170/w:1024/p:16x9/Russie-Ukraine-Kertch-Info-Verif-Une.png">© Captures d'écran/ Montage RFI</source><dc:creator>Grégory Genevrier</dc:creator></item><item><category>Europe</category><title>«C'est un jour historique»: en Serbie, le mouvement des étudiants fait son entrée au Parlement</title><link>https://www.rfi.fr/fr/europe/20261117-c-est-un-jour-historique-en-serbie-le-mouvement-des-%C3%A9tudiants-fait-son-entr%C3%A9e-au-parlement</link><description>
Ce mardi 17 novembre marque la première session du Parlement nouvellement élu en Serbie, qui consacre la victoire de la liste étudiante après deux ans de manifestations anticorruption.
</description><media:thumbnail url="https://s.rfi.fr/media/display/73fb2964-e278-11f1-a3a1-ff16da94d1fe/w:1024/p:16x9/2026-11-17T092505Z-1014948375-RC2LPOAZ0JM3-RTRMADP-3-SERBIA-PARLIAMENT.jpg"/><enclosure url="https://s.rfi.fr/media/display/73fb2964-e278-11f1-a3a1-ff16da94d1fe/w:1024/p:16x9/2026-11-17T092505Z-1014948375-RC2LPOAZ0JM3-RTRMADP-3-SERBIA-PARLIAMENT.jpg" type="image/jpeg" length="0"/><guid isPermaLink="false">2c2f50a0-e279-11f1-97b9-0be1f30c0e1f</guid><pubDate>Tue, 17 Nov 2026 12:33:30 GMT</pubDate><source url="https://s.rfi.fr/media/display/73fb2964-e278-11f1-a3a1-ff16da94d1fe/w:1024/p:16x9/2026-11-17T092505Z-1014948375-RC2LPOAZ0JM3-RTRMADP-3-SERBIA-PARLIAMENT.jpg">© Zorana Jevtic / Reuters</source><dc:creator>RFI</dc:creator></item><item><category>Europe</category><title>Soldats français déployés en Ukraine: Moscou y voit une «participation directe» au conflit</title><link>https://www.rfi.fr/fr/europe/20261117-soldats-fran%C3%A7ais-d%C3%A9ploy%C3%A9s-en-ukraine-moscou-y-voit-une-participation-directe-au-conflit</link><description>
Ce mardi 17 novembre, le ministre russe des Affaires étrangères a qualifié de « participation directe » au conflit en Ukraine le déploiement de soldats français opérant en Ukraine pour des missions de formation et d'entretien de matériels, révélé lundi par RFI.
</description><media:thumbnail url="https://s.rfi.fr/media/display/5112e664-3a74-11f1-904f-005056a97e36/w:1024/p:16x9/AP26062382346034.jpg"/><enclosure url="https://s.rfi.fr/media/display/5112e664-3a74-11f1-904f-005056a97e36/w:1024/p:16x9/AP26062382346034.jpg" type="image/jpeg" length="0"/><guid isPermaLink="false">cc8b09f6-e277-11f1-9c03-0f08de7ca9eb</guid><pubDate>Tue, 17 Nov 2026 11:14:54 GMT</pubDate><source url="https://s.rfi.fr/media/display/5112e664-3a74-11f1-904f-005056a97e36/w:1024/p:16x9/AP26062382346034.jpg">© Pavel Bednyakov/AP</source><dc:creator>RFI</dc:creator></item><item><category>Appels sur l'actualité</category><title>Guerre en Ukraine : que cache la mission secrète des militaires français?</title><link>https://www.rfi.fr/fr/podcasts/appels-sur-l-actualit%C3%A9/20261117-guerre-en-ukraine-que-cache-la-mission-secr%C3%A8te-des-militaires-fran%C3%A7ais</link><description>
C’est une information RFI : des soldats français sont présents en Ukraine depuis l’été dernier. Selon notre enquête, ils sont réunis au sein d’un dispositif confidentiel baptisé « Volia ». Leur mission : former des militaires ukrainiens pour assurer la maintenance des équipements livrés par Paris, notamment les canons Caesar et les avions Mirage 2000. Ils ne prennent pas part aux combats. La France n’a toutefois pas confirmé officiellement l’existence de cette mission. Pourquoi cette opération n’a-t-elle pas été portée à la connaissance du Parlement ? Et comment la Russie peut-elle interpréter cette présence militaire française sur le sol ukrainien ?
</description><media:thumbnail url="https://s.rfi.fr/media/display/1ef1b610-e01e-11f1-9b8c-695cb59fade5/w:1024/p:16x9/000-Par8194826.jpg"/><enclosure url="https://s.rfi.fr/media/display/1ef1b610-e01e-11f1-9b8c-695cb59fade5/w:1024/p:16x9/000-Par8194826.jpg" type="image/jpeg" length="0"/><guid isPermaLink="false">6edbc838-e1ad-11f1-9213-e1d07338c648</guid><pubDate>Tue, 17 Nov 2026 09:00:19 GMT</pubDate><dc:creator>Juan Gomez</dc:creator></item><item><category>Appels sur l'actualité</category><title>Guerre en Ukraine : 400 000 Russes morts sur le front?</title><link>https://www.rfi.fr/fr/podcasts/appels-sur-l-actualit%C3%A9/20261117-guerre-en-ukraine-400-000-russes-morts-sur-le-front</link><description>
Près de 400 000 soldats russes auraient péri depuis le début de la guerre en Ukraine. C’est ce que révèlent des documents attribués à l’institut de statistiques russe Rosstat, dont deux groupes de hackers affirment avoir piraté les données. Des révélations particulièrement sensibles, alors que Vladimir Poutine a classé les informations sur les pertes militaires au secret d’État dès 2015. Comment ces hackers ont-ils pu accéder à ces données ? Ces chiffres sont-ils vraiment crédibles ?
</description><media:thumbnail url="https://s.rfi.fr/media/display/12463d34-9854-11ed-bc0b-005056a90284/w:1024/p:16x9/AP23003562030298.jpg"/><enclosure url="https://s.rfi.fr/media/display/12463d34-9854-11ed-bc0b-005056a90284/w:1024/p:16x9/AP23003562030298.jpg" type="image/jpeg" length="0"/><guid isPermaLink="false">1e6ce9c6-e1ae-11f1-823e-1b46fca9b9c5</guid><pubDate>Tue, 17 Nov 2026 08:56:28 GMT</pubDate><dc:creator>Juan Gomez</dc:creator></item><item><category>Europe</category><title>Nouvel échange de frappes entre la Russie et l'Ukraine, deux morts en Crimée</title><link>https://www.rfi.fr/fr/europe/20261117-la-russie-frappe-deux-ponts-majeurs-%C3%A0-kiev-l-ukraine-cible-%C3%A0-nouveau-la-crim%C3%A9e</link><description>

</description><media:thumbnail url="https://s.rfi.fr/media/display/63468264-e253-11f1-9b57-29048b396e03/w:1024/p:16x9/000-D7KG3CQ.jpg"/><enclosure url="https://s.rfi.fr/media/display/63468264-e253-11f1-9b57-29048b396e03/w:1024/p:16x9/000-D7KG3CQ.jpg" type="image/jpeg" length="0"/><guid isPermaLink="false">95f153a6-e253-11f1-b160-a15f137c0baa</guid><pubDate>Tue, 17 Nov 2026 06:54:32 GMT</pubDate><source url="https://s.rfi.fr/media/display/63468264-e253-11f1-9b57-29048b396e03/w:1024/p:16x9/000-D7KG3CQ.jpg">AFP - STRINGER</source><dc:creator>RFI avec AFP</dc:creator></item><item><category>Accents d'Europe</category><title>Sur les traces des personnes réduites en esclavage</title><link>https://www.rfi.fr/fr/podcasts/accents-d-europe/20261116-sur-les-traces-des-personnes-r%C3%A9duites-en-esclavage</link><description>
Donner un nom, une histoire, à des millions d’asservis et comprendre l’impact de la traite sur les inégalités d’aujourd’hui : dans cette émission, on ouvre les registres britanniques de l’esclavage.
</description><media:thumbnail url="https://s.rfi.fr/media/display/25b7ccb2-02c6-11ed-b799-005056bfa79e/w:1024/p:16x9/AP17198587355318.jpg"/><enclosure url="https://s.rfi.fr/media/display/25b7ccb2-02c6-11ed-b799-005056bfa79e/w:1024/p:16x9/AP17198587355318.jpg" type="image/jpeg" length="0"/><guid isPermaLink="false">d9124e66-e1f8-11f1-bfcd-390d5e1d14eb</guid><pubDate>Mon, 16 Nov 2026 21:20:57 GMT</pubDate><dc:creator>Juliette Gheerbrant</dc:creator></item><item><category>Europe</category><title>Espagne: Lula da Silva soutient Pedro Sanchez avant les législatives anticipées du 29 novembre</title><link>https://www.rfi.fr/fr/europe/20261116-espagne-lula-da-silva-soutient-pedro-sanchez-avant-les-l%C3%A9gislatives-anticip%C3%A9es-du-29-novembre</link><description>
Le Premier ministre espagnol Pedro Sanchez a reçu, lundi 16 novembre, le soutien du président brésilien Lula da Silva à Madrid, à moins de deux semaines des élections législatives anticipées du 29 novembre. </description><media:thumbnail url="https://s.rfi.fr/media/display/6c241fe8-e1e7-11f1-90be-f71d22e7fea9/w:1024/p:16x9/AP26320393432966.jpg"/><enclosure url="https://s.rfi.fr/media/display/6c241fe8-e1e7-11f1-90be-f71d22e7fea9/w:1024/p:16x9/AP26320393432966.jpg" type="image/jpeg" length="0"/><guid isPermaLink="false">ac6cf11e-e1e8-11f1-bb05-5d0ba7174a9f</guid><pubDate>Mon, 16 Nov 2026 18:53:42 GMT</pubDate><source url="https://s.rfi.fr/media/display/6c241fe8-e1e7-11f1-90be-f71d22e7fea9/w:1024/p:16x9/AP26320393432966.jpg">© AP Photo/Francisco Seco</source><dc:creator>RFI</dc:creator></item><item><category>Europe</category><title>Soldats français en Ukraine: «Cela va sans doute amplifier la réaction de propagande de la Russie»</title><link>https://www.rfi.fr/fr/europe/20261116-soldats-fran%C3%A7ais-en-ukraine-cela-va-sans-doute-amplifier-la-r%C3%A9action-de-propagande-de-la-russie</link><description>

Cinq pays européens défendent une politique migratoire très ferme et pilotent ensemble un projet visant à envoyer des migrants dans des centres situés hors d’Europe. Après des mois de réflexion, ils ont retenu le Rwanda pour un premier projet pilote, dont l’ouverture est prévue en 2027.
</description><media:thumbnail url="https://s.rfi.fr/media/display/013e2372-e1d3-11f1-80e8-f71d22e7fea9/w:1024/p:16x9/AP26320558302536.jpg"/><enclosure url="https://s.rfi.fr/media/display/013e2372-e1d3-11f1-80e8-f71d22e7fea9/w:1024/p:16x9/AP26320558302536.jpg" type="image/jpeg" length="0"/><guid isPermaLink="false">bff09a3a-e1d2-11f1-86ed-abe06ccee855</guid><pubDate>Mon, 16 Nov 2026 15:35:36 GMT</pubDate><source url="https://s.rfi.fr/media/display/013e2372-e1d3-11f1-80e8-f71d22e7fea9/w:1024/p:16x9/AP26320558302536.jpg">AP Photo/Heinz-Peter Bader - Heinz-Peter Bader</source><dc:creator>RFI avec AFP</dc:creator></item><item><category>Invité international</category><title>Soldats français en Ukraine: «Nous ne sommes pas cobelligérants», rappelle le sénateur PS Rachid Temal</title><link>https://www.rfi.fr/fr/podcasts/invit%C3%A9-international/20261116-soldats-fran%C3%A7ais-en-ukraine-nous-ne-sommes-pas-cobellig%C3%A9rants-rappelle-le-s%C3%A9nateur-ps-rachid-temal</link><description>

</description><media:thumbnail url="https://s.rfi.fr/media/display/dd94df9c-ae02-11f0-a21b-005056a97e36/w:1024/p:16x9/Ukraine-Soldats-Armee-Russie-Guerre.jpg"/><enclosure url="https://s.rfi.fr/media/display/dd94df9c-ae02-11f0-a21b-005056a97e36/w:1024/p:16x9/Ukraine-Soldats-Armee-Russie-Guerre.jpg" type="image/jpeg" length="0"/><guid isPermaLink="false">dc79170e-e1c8-11f1-9f22-1b5d0dc6ca69</guid><pubDate>Mon, 16 Nov 2026 15:03:55 GMT</pubDate><dc:creator>Candice Mazaud-Tomazic</dc:creator></item><item><category>Europe</category><title>Belgique: le roi Philippe accorde une semaine de plus à Bart De Wever pour boucler le budget</title><link>https://www.rfi.fr/fr/europe/20261116-belgique-le-roi-philippe-accorde-une-semaine-de-plus-%C3%A0-bart-de-wever-pour-boucler-le-budget</link><description>
Le Premier ministre belge a dû partager le constat que les négociations sur le budget n'aboutissent toujours pas au sein de sa coalition. </description><media:thumbnail url="https://s.rfi.fr/media/display/81eb9b82-e06e-11f1-a32c-f71d22e7fea9/w:1024/p:16x9/AP26280291105956.jpg"/><enclosure url="https://s.rfi.fr/media/display/81eb9b82-e06e-11f1-a32c-f71d22e7fea9/w:1024/p:16x9/AP26280291105956.jpg" type="image/jpeg" length="0"/><guid isPermaLink="false">ec11b566-e049-11f1-a0f7-b9a889b5d5a2</guid><pubDate>Mon, 16 Nov 2026 13:57:21 GMT</pubDate><source url="https://s.rfi.fr/media/display/81eb9b82-e06e-11f1-a32c-f71d22e7fea9/w:1024/p:16x9/AP26280291105956.jpg">© Markus Schreiber / AP Photo</source><dc:creator>Christophe Drevet</dc:creator></item><item><category>Europe</category><title>Les affaires de violences sexuelles impliquant Russell Brand et David Walliams secouent le Royaume-Uni</title><link>https://www.rfi.fr/fr/europe/20261116-les-affaires-de-violences-sexuelles-impliquant-russell-brand-et-david-walliams-secouent-le-royaume-uni</link><description>

</description><media:thumbnail url="https://s.rfi.fr/media/display/2c77cbc6-df24-11f1-a56b-3f371022a770/w:1024/p:16x9/AP26316808764019.jpg"/><enclosure url="https://s.rfi.fr/media/display/2c77cbc6-df24-11f1-a56b-3f371022a770/w:1024/p:16x9/AP26316808764019.jpg" type="image/jpeg" length="0"/><guid isPermaLink="false">0e291278-df61-11f1-9ecc-33767f4b6941</guid><pubDate>Mon, 16 Nov 2026 09:05:18 GMT</pubDate><dc:creator>Juan Gomez</dc:creator></item><item><category>Europe</category><title>L'Ukraine frappe le pont reliant la Russie à la Crimée annexée par Moscou</title><link>https://www.rfi.fr/fr/europe/20261116-l-ukraine-frappe-le-pont-reliant-la-russie-%C3%A0-la-crim%C3%A9e-annex%C3%A9e-par-moscou</link><description>
L'Ukraine a « frappé » le pont reliant la Russie à la péninsule de Crimée annexée par Moscou en 2014, restreignant la circulation sur cet ouvrage stratégique, a annoncé lundi 16 novembre le chef des autorités locales nommé par Moscou.
</description><media:thumbnail url="https://s.rfi.fr/media/display/e6618ed8-e18f-11f1-a857-f71d22e7fea9/w:1024/p:16x9/000-D7KG3ZQ.jpg"/><enclosure url="https://s.rfi.fr/media/display/e6618ed8-e18f-11f1-a857-f71d22e7fea9/w:1024/p:16x9/000-D7KG3ZQ.jpg" type="image/jpeg" length="0"/><guid isPermaLink="false">1f94f66c-e191-11f1-95aa-5b9e7bed2e56</guid><pubDate>Mon, 16 Nov 2026 07:42:37 GMT</pubDate><source url="https://s.rfi.fr/media/display/e6618ed8-e18f-11f1-a857-f71d22e7fea9/w:1024/p:16x9/000-D7KG3ZQ.jpg">© AFP - STRINGER</source><dc:creator>RFI avec AFP</dc:creator></item><item><category>Europe</category><title>Mission «Volia»: comment l'armée française opère en Ukraine</title><link>https://www.rfi.fr/fr/europe/20261116-mission-volia-comment-l-arm%C3%A9e-fran%C3%A7aise-op%C3%A8re-en-ukraine</link><description>
Paris n'a jamais confirmé la présence de militaires français sur le sol ukrainien. Or, selon plusieurs interlocuteurs joints par RFI, un soutien militaire français joue un rôle actif dans le pays depuis au moins l'été 2026.
</description><media:thumbnail url="https://s.rfi.fr/media/display/1ef1b610-e01e-11f1-9b8c-695cb59fade5/w:1024/p:16x9/000-Par8194826.jpg"/><enclosure url="https://s.rfi.fr/media/display/1ef1b610-e01e-11f1-9b8c-695cb59fade5/w:1024/p:16x9/000-Par8194826.jpg" type="image/jpeg" length="0"/><guid isPermaLink="false">6fc6cbc2-e012-11f1-96bb-d5c8a7614a7b</guid><pubDate>Mon, 16 Nov 2026 04:59:35 GMT</pubDate><source url="https://s.rfi.fr/media/display/1ef1b610-e01e-11f1-9b8c-695cb59fade5/w:1024/p:16x9/000-Par8194826.jpg">AFP - MARTIN BUREAU</source><dc:creator>Franck Alexandre</dc:creator></item><item><category>Reportage international</category><title>Au Royaume-Uni, des archives inédites pour retrouver les ancêtres victimes de l'esclavage</title><link>https://www.rfi.fr/fr/podcasts/reportage-international/20261115-au-royaume-uni-des-archives-in%C3%A9dites-pour-retrouver-les-anc%C3%AAtres-victimes-de-l-esclavage</link><description>
À Londres, au Royaume-Uni, des universités ont compilé et mis en ligne des archives pour créer un registre des personnes réduites en esclavage par les Britanniques dans leurs colonies, jusqu'au XIXe siècle. Jusqu'à présent, les registres disponibles identifiaient les propriétaires de plantations et de personnes asservies. C'est la première fois que sont rassemblées et publiées des informations détaillées sur les victimes de la traite transatlantique. Ces archives sont exceptionnelles : elles représentent une source précieuse pour les historiens, mais aussi pour tous les descendants qui cherchent à connaître leurs ancêtres et leur histoire.
</description><media:thumbnail url="https://s.rfi.fr/media/display/a8857c74-6ca9-11f1-9b88-005056a90284/w:1024/p:16x9/000-972Z7PA.jpg"/><enclosure url="https://s.rfi.fr/media/display/a8857c74-6ca9-11f1-9b88-005056a90284/w:1024/p:16x9/000-972Z7PA.jpg" type="image/jpeg" length="0"/><guid isPermaLink="false">580fc43e-e12a-11f1-accf-5ba32673de97</guid><pubDate>Sun, 15 Nov 2026 23:02:19 GMT</pubDate><dc:creator>Marie Billon</dc:creator></item><item><category>Europe</category><title>République tchèque: 400 000 manifestants à Prague contre la réforme de l'audiovisuel public</title><link>https://www.rfi.fr/fr/europe/20261115-r%C3%A9publique-tch%C3%A8que-400-000-manifestants-%C3%A0-prague-contre-la-r%C3%A9forme-de-l-audiovisuel-public</link><description>
Une importante manifestation s'est tenue, dimanche 15 novembre à Prague, en République tchèque, contre le gouvernement du milliardaire Andrej Babis et son projet de suppression de la redevance audiovisuelle. Selon les organisateurs, environ 400 000 personnes ont participé au rassemblement, l'un des plus importants de ces dernières décennies dans le pays.
</description><media:thumbnail url="https://s.rfi.fr/media/display/ad2652d8-e122-11f1-9e81-f71d22e7fea9/w:1024/p:16x9/AP26319502635204.jpg"/><enclosure url="https://s.rfi.fr/media/display/ad2652d8-e122-11f1-9e81-f71d22e7fea9/w:1024/p:16x9/AP26319502635204.jpg" type="image/jpeg" length="0"/><guid isPermaLink="false">f4aa4bf2-e125-11f1-a93b-1187dfff2b00</guid><pubDate>Sun, 15 Nov 2026 20:42:41 GMT</pubDate><source url="https://s.rfi.fr/media/display/ad2652d8-e122-11f1-9e81-f71d22e7fea9/w:1024/p:16x9/AP26319502635204.jpg">© MICHAELA RIHOVA/CTK via AP</source><dc:creator>RFI</dc:creator></item><item><category>Europe</category><title>Pays-Bas: des avions perdent le signal GPS dans le ciel, des bateaux russes en mer du Nord suspectés</title><link>https://www.rfi.fr/fr/europe/20261115-pays-bas-des-avions-perdent-le-signal-gps-dans-le-ciel-des-bateaux-russes-en-mer-du-nord-suspect%C3%A9s</link><description>
Que s'est-il passé, exactement, dans le ciel néerlandais, lundi 9 novembre ? Ce jour-là, des dizaines d'avion survolant les Pays-Bas ont perdu le signal GPS. Une perturbation des systèmes de navigation qui serait liée à la présence d'un navire russe dans les eaux de la mer du Nord.
</description><media:thumbnail url="https://s.rfi.fr/media/display/4b9d5f26-e126-11f1-a0ae-f71d22e7fea9/w:1024/p:16x9/PAYS-BAS-AVIONS-AMSTERDAM-SCHIPOL.jpg"/><enclosure url="https://s.rfi.fr/media/display/4b9d5f26-e126-11f1-a0ae-f71d22e7fea9/w:1024/p:16x9/PAYS-BAS-AVIONS-AMSTERDAM-SCHIPOL.jpg" type="image/jpeg" length="0"/><guid isPermaLink="false">55e5b604-e126-11f1-969e-7f883c542106</guid><pubDate>Sun, 15 Nov 2026 18:57:06 GMT</pubDate><source url="https://s.rfi.fr/media/display/4b9d5f26-e126-11f1-a0ae-f71d22e7fea9/w:1024/p:16x9/PAYS-BAS-AVIONS-AMSTERDAM-SCHIPOL.jpg">AFP - ALEXANDER KLEIN</source><dc:creator>RFI</dc:creator></item><item><category>Europe</category><title>L'Estonie va fermer sa frontière avec la Russie après une tentative de sabotage contre une usine de drones</title><link>https://www.rfi.fr/fr/europe/20261115-l-estonie-va-fermer-sa-fronti%C3%A8re-avec-la-russie-apr%C3%A8s-une-tentative-de-sabotage-contre-une-usine-de-drones</link><description>
L'Estonie a annoncé, dimanche 15 novembre 2026, qu'elle allait entièrement fermer sa frontière avec la Russie après avoir déjoué in extremis une tentative d'incendie d'une usine de drones, orchestrée selon elle par le renseignement militaire russe GRU. La fermeture est prévue au 1er décembre.
</description><media:thumbnail url="https://s.rfi.fr/media/display/38be082a-e116-11f1-82f3-3f371022a770/w:1024/p:16x9/AP26130376881847.jpg"/><enclosure url="https://s.rfi.fr/media/display/38be082a-e116-11f1-82f3-3f371022a770/w:1024/p:16x9/AP26130376881847.jpg" type="image/jpeg" length="0"/><guid isPermaLink="false">29878ab2-e115-11f1-acd0-df1bc2f83c61</guid><pubDate>Sun, 15 Nov 2026 17:25:04 GMT</pubDate><source url="https://s.rfi.fr/media/display/38be082a-e116-11f1-82f3-3f371022a770/w:1024/p:16x9/AP26130376881847.jpg">AP - Sergei Grits</source><dc:creator>RFI avec AFP</dc:creator></item><item><category>Europe</category><title>Expulsions vers des pays tiers: ce que l’on sait du projet de «hubs de retour» préparé par cinq États européens</title><link>https://www.rfi.fr/fr/europe/20261115-expulsions-vers-des-pays-tiers-ce-que-l-on-sait-du-projet-pr%C3%A9par%C3%A9-par-cinq-%C3%A9tats-europ%C3%A9en</link><description>
Allemagne, Autriche, Danemark, Grèce et Pays-Bas veulent pouvoir transférer hors de l'Union européenne certaines personnes sous le coup d'une décision de retour. À la veille d'une réunion à Vienne, où le Rwanda devrait être présenté comme premier pays partenaire, RFI fait le point sur un projet qui suscite beaucoup de questions.
</description><media:thumbnail url="https://s.rfi.fr/media/display/549900c6-e0cc-11f1-be6d-f71d22e7fea9/w:1024/p:16x9/000-C7CK3JE.jpg"/><enclosure url="https://s.rfi.fr/media/display/549900c6-e0cc-11f1-be6d-f71d22e7fea9/w:1024/p:16x9/000-C7CK3JE.jpg" type="image/jpeg" length="0"/><guid isPermaLink="false">d2532b3a-dc1d-11f1-8af2-77d60eb72c13</guid><pubDate>Sun, 15 Nov 2026 14:52:30 GMT</pubDate><source url="https://s.rfi.fr/media/display/549900c6-e0cc-11f1-be6d-f71d22e7fea9/w:1024/p:16x9/000-C7CK3JE.jpg">AFP - LISELOTTE SABROE</source><dc:creator>Aurore Lartigue</dc:creator></item><item><category>Europe</category><title>Que pensent les Ukrainiens de la proposition d'échanger le Donbass contre l'intégration à l'Otan?</title><link>https://www.rfi.fr/fr/europe/20261115-que-pensent-les-ukrainiens-de-la-proposition-d-%C3%A9changer-le-donbass-contre-l-int%C3%A9gration-%C3%A0-l-otan</link><description>
Céder le Donbass à la Russie contre une adhésion de l’Ukraine à l’Otan : c’est l’idée proposée à Volodymyr Zelensky par les émissaires américains à l'issue des négociations entre Washington, Moscou et Kiev la semaine dernière. C’est la première fois qu’une telle piste est évoquée. Le président ukrainien ne s’y opposerait pas mais voudrait passer par un référendum, même si cette piste n’est pas franchement prise au sérieux en Ukraine.
</description><media:thumbnail url="https://s.rfi.fr/media/display/409711e6-e0e8-11f1-9a6f-f71d22e7fea9/w:1024/p:16x9/AP26316810454758.jpg"/><enclosure url="https://s.rfi.fr/media/display/409711e6-e0e8-11f1-9a6f-f71d22e7fea9/w:1024/p:16x9/AP26316810454758.jpg" type="image/jpeg" length="0"/><guid isPermaLink="false">33c55c86-e0eb-11f1-b040-831c6b3bf57d</guid><pubDate>Sun, 15 Nov 2026 12:08:21 GMT</pubDate><source url="https://s.rfi.fr/media/display/409711e6-e0e8-11f1-9a6f-f71d22e7fea9/w:1024/p:16x9/AP26316810454758.jpg">© Peter Morrison / AP</source><dc:creator>RFI</dc:creator></item></channel></rss>

C'est le plus récent piratage informatique d'une société française : Maileva, filiale de La Poste, s'est vu dérober les coordonnées de 22 millions de clients (nom, prénom et adresse postale). Elle est la dernière victime d'une longue liste de victimes de cyberattaques en France, après le Crédit Mutuel Arkéa la semaine dernière, le Trésor public l'été dernier ou les frigos de supermarchés les 11 et 12 octobre. En 2025, la CNIL a compté 6 000 violations de données, en hausse de 50% sur 3 ans.
</description><media:thumbnail url="https://s.france24.com/media/display/42cd69b6-e1eb-11f1-9f5b-3f371022a770/w:1024/p:16x9/XX-NW-OOV-ECO-MAILEVA-PIRATAGE-MANENT-Laure-transfer.png"/><enclosure url="https://s.france24.com/media/display/42cd69b6-e1eb-11f1-9f5b-3f371022a770/w:1024/p:16x9/XX-NW-OOV-ECO-MAILEVA-PIRATAGE-MANENT-Laure-transfer.png" type="image/png" length="0"/><guid isPermaLink="false">9ae3095c-e1f6-11f1-8c1d-7bc933339a1c</guid><pubDate>Mon, 16 Nov 2026 19:57:51 GMT</pubDate><dc:creator>Laure MANENT</dc:creator></item><item><category>Info éco</category><title>Francophonie : une puissance économique encore sous-exploitée</title><link>https://www.france24.com/fr/%C3%A9missions/info-%C3%A9co/20261116-francophonie-une-puissance-%C3%A9conomique-encore-sous-exploit%C3%A9e</link><description>
